title: What's next for beloved candy shop after heartbreaking accident - NewsBreak
text:
By Payton Cavanaugh ,
59 minutes ago
HOOSICK FALLS, N.Y. ( NEWS10 )– One person was treated for serious injuries early Monday evening after crashing into a local mom & pop restaurant and candy store. For the owners, Tammy and Charlie Morgan, the business means absolutely everything. They have spent nearly half of their lives bringing smiles, warmth, and kindness to their community. In the wake of this accident, they promise to re-open when the time is right, and they’ve followed all the proper steps to clean up the aftermath.
“We’re devastated, but we know there’s two families involved, us and the other people,” Tammy explained. “We pray for the gentleman that, thank God, by the grace of God, is alive.”
Tammy noted that the holiday season is one of the most important times of the year for the candy business, and this is hitting them hard.
“This month is pretty much how we survive January and February, so I’m not going to lie, we’re worried,” noted Tammy.
Tammy and Charlie have spent the last thirty one years hand-making and serving everything from chocolates, to caramels, and even two pound burgers. Tammy makes the sweets, Charlie cooks the savory, and their main goal is to make everyone who walks through their door feel comfortable and welcomed.
Download our WTEN+ streaming app on Roku, Fire TV and Apple TV! “We want you to feel at home,” Tammy noted. “We’re not a chain restaurant. We don’t want to be. We’re a mom and pop restaurant. I’ll walk you to your car, if it’s dark or cold. I mean, our customers are like family.”
Tammy’s Candy Kettle feels like a trip to your grandparent’s kitchen, and that’s because it’s their home. Living in the same building as their business, they said they’re always at work, but they wouldn’t have it any other way.
“We live upstairs, we always have, so it made it easy to go to work, but it didn’t feel like work,” noted Tammy. “It’s home, it’s everything. I could work fourteen hours a day and go to bed and not wait to get started again. I love my husband. We love what we do. We can’t be without this business, our families are gone. This is why we exist.”
Get the latest news, weather, sports and entertainment delivered right to your inbox! Tammy said they are no stranger to hard times, but that’s what makes their love for their business even stronger. From losing both of their parents, to navigating business during the pandemic, and Charlie’s recovery from a life-altering stroke, they continued to push forward.
“Getting this place going again is what drove him to be able to get up,” Tammy explained. “He lost the left side, but he’s cooking and he’s doing it with one hand.”
On December eighth, when the accident happened, they faced yet another obstacle. That night, an individual drove his vehicle straight into the store front, and was airlifted to Albany Medical Center with serious injuries. That accident damaged nearly every display case, shelf, window, and pounds of confections.
“I was standing behind that candy case probably fifteen times during the day that day,” Tammy noted. “But thank God I wasn’t there at that moment in time, or I don’t believe I would be here today.”
Yet, even with all of the work to be done, Charlie and Tammy were most concerned for the family of the man in the vehicle. They expressed immense gratitude that despite the horrific circumstances, nobody was killed.
“We’re devastated, but I have to take it one step at a time,” Tammy stated. “I have to keep things in perspective that the most important thing is that the man lived.”
For those left wondering about the future of Tammy’s Candy Kettle, they want you to know that they are not going anywhere, and they’re planning a grand re-opening in the future.
“My husband always said to me when we went through hard times, our motto is failure is not an option,” Tammy added. “So we’ll get through this somehow. I need more years in my life, more hours in a day, because I just love it so much. I always said, when God decides that it’s my time to go, I just hope I’m in there making candy when it happens.”
